identity.name: Phosphates
identity.chemical_class: Inorganic salts of calcium and phosphate

function.mechanism: Absorbs moisture and prevents clumping in powders; provides bioavailable Ca^2+ when used as fortifier.

efsa.status: No specific ADI; considered safe within current use levels
efsa.key_finding: No adverse effects observed up to industrial intake levels.

concerns.summary: High chronic phosphate intake (>2 g/day) linked to kidney stones and CKD progression.
Excess Ca phosphate may displace native bone mineral, potentially reducing bone density.
Short-term ingestion >200 mg produced mild nausea in a few volunteers.
No systemic hypersensitivity reported; occasional irritant dermatitis in workers handling dust.

adi_exceedance.notes: Typical exposure well below provisional ADI (1 g/day). Children <5 with high cereal intake may approach ADI threshold.

risk_assessment.rationale: Accepted by EFSA, FDA GRAS, and JECFA with established ADI; only moderate concerns at very high doses.

sources.title: EFSA Scientific Opinion on Food Additives in the EU
IARC Monographs on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans
